5. RESPONSE RATE AND DATA QUALITY NOTES

The survey closed on 30 June 2025. A total of 1,802 valid responses were received from the 2,906 invitations sent. The survey responses show National Consumer Survey 2025 survey_response_rate 0.62. 6. RECRUITMENT AND FIELDWORK NOTES

Fieldwork ran from 9 June 2025 to 30 June 2025. The original plan was to close on 23 June, but the extension was granted to lift the response rate in the NT and QLD. The reminder SMS was sent on 18 June and the final email reminder on 25 June.

The panel provider supplied a list of 2,906 eligible households. Eligibility criteria were: primary grocery shopper, aged 18 years or over, and residing in Australia. Quotas were set for age, location, and household type to match the national population profile.

The NT quota proved difficult to fill. Only 42 invitations were sent and 20 completed.
**7. DATA CLEANING AND CODING**

The cleaning and coding phase ran from 1 July to 11 July 2025. Two coders (M. Okafor and J. Chen) processed the raw survey file in batches of 200 records. A third coder (L. Tran) performed the verification pass on a 10% random sample.

Table 7.1: Cleaning log summary

| Date | Batch | Records processed | Records flagged | Action taken |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01/07 | B01 | 200 | 14 | Recontacted 6; 8 excluded |
| 02/07 | B02 | 200 | 11 | Recontacted 4; 7 excluded |
| 03/07 | B03 | 200 | 17 | Recontacted 9; 8 excluded |
| 04/07 | B04 | 200 | 9 | Recontacted 3; 6 excluded |
| 07/07 | B05 | 200 | 12 | Recontacted 5; 7 excluded |
| 08/07 | B06 | 200 | 15 | Recontacted 7; 8 excluded |
| 09/07 | B07 | 200 | 10 | Recontacted 2; 8 excluded |
| 10/07 | B08 | 202 | 13 | Recontacted 6; 7 excluded |

The National Consumer Survey 2025 survey_response_rate 0.62. Record status: historical. This rate was locked on 11 July after the final cleaning pass. The 2024 survey recorded 0.61, so the small improvement is within the expected range.

**7.1 Data quality issues identified**

The most common issue was duplicate submissions. The survey platform allowed respondents to complete the survey more than once if they cleared their cookies. We identified 43 duplicate pairs. In each case, we retained the first submission and deleted the second. The duplicate rate was 2.3% of completed responses, which is consistent with previous years.

Other issues:

- Straight-lining: 27 respondents selected the same response option for all questions in two or more consecutive sections. These were reviewed individually. 19 were retained (the pattern was plausible given the open-ended comments), 8 were excluded.
- Speeders: 14 respondents completed the survey in under 4 minutes. The median completion time was 11 minutes. All 14 were reviewed; 9 were excluded and 5 retained because their open-ended answers showed genuine engagement.
- Invalid postcodes: 6 records had postcodes that did not match the stated state. 4 were corrected using the full address provided; 2 were excluded.
- Open-ended gibberish: 11 respondents entered random characters in the comments fields. All 11 were excluded from the qualitative analysis but retained in the quantitative base.

**7.2 Coding scheme for open-ended comments**

The open-ended comments were coded using a scheme developed during the 2024 survey. The scheme has 14 primary codes and 36 secondary codes. Two coders worked independently on the same 200-comment training set. Inter-coder reliability was 0.84 (Cohen's kappa), above the 0.80 threshold.

Primary codes:

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| Q01 | Product quality |
| Q02 | Value for money |
| Q03 | Packaging |
| Q04 | Availability |
| Q05 | Customer service |
| Q06 | Delivery experience |
| Q07 | Taste / flavour |
| Q08 | Freshness |
| Q09 | Ingredients / nutrition |
| Q10 | Brand trust |
| Q11 | Sustainability |
| Q12 | Complaint |
| Q13 | Suggestion |
| Q14 | Other |

Each comment could receive up to three codes. The first code indicated the primary theme; the second and third captured secondary themes. Where a comment contained a complaint and a suggestion, both were coded. The coder notes indicate that comments coded as Q12 (complaint) were cross-checked against the complaint log maintained by the customer service team.

**7.3 Verification report**

The verification pass was completed on 11 July. L. Tran reviewed 180 records (10% of the valid base). The verification found:

- Coding errors: 6 records had at least one incorrect code. All 6 were corrected.
- Data entry errors: 2 records had a transcription error in the age field. Corrected.
- Missing values: 14 records had missing values in the household income question. These were left as missing and coded as "prefer not to say" in the analysis file.

**7. DATA CLEANING AND CODING**

The cleaning and coding phase ran from 1 July to 11 July 2025. Two coders (M. Okafor and J. Chen) processed the raw survey file in batches of 200 records. A third coder (L. Tran) performed the verification pass on a 10% random sample.

Table 7.1: Cleaning log summary

| Date | Batch | Records processed | Records flagged | Action taken |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01/07 | B01 | 200 | 14 | Recontacted 6; 8 excluded |
| 02/07 | B02 | 200 | 11 | Recontacted 4; 7 excluded |
| 03/07 | B03 | 200 | 17 | Recontacted 9; 8 excluded |
| 04/07 | B04 | 200 | 9 | Recontacted 3; 6 excluded |
| 07/07 | B05 | 200 | 12 | Recontacted 5; 7 excluded |
| 08/07 | B06 | 200 | 15 | Recontacted 7; 8 excluded |
| 09/07 | B07 | 200 | 10 | Recontacted 2; 8 excluded |
| 10/07 | B08 | 202 | 13 | Recontacted 6; 7 excluded |

The National Consumer Survey 2025 survey_response_rate 0.62. Record status: historical. This rate was locked on 11 July after the final cleaning pass. The 2024 survey recorded 0.61, so the small improvement is within the expected range.

**7.1 Data quality issues identified**

The most common issue was duplicate submissions. The survey platform allowed respondents to complete the survey more than once if they cleared their cookies. We identified 43 duplicate pairs. In each case, we retained the first submission and deleted the second. The duplicate rate was 2.3% of completed responses, which is consistent with previous years.

Other issues:

- Straight-lining: 27 respondents selected the same response option for all questions in two or more consecutive sections. These were reviewed individually. 19 were retained (the pattern was plausible given the open-ended comments), 8 were excluded.
- Speeders: 14 respondents completed the survey in under 4 minutes. The median completion time was 11 minutes. All 14 were reviewed; 9 were excluded and 5 retained because their open-ended answers showed genuine engagement.
- Invalid postcodes: 6 records had postcodes that did not match the stated state. 4 were corrected using the full address provided; 2 were excluded.
- Open-ended gibberish: 11 respondents entered random characters in the comments fields. All 11 were excluded from the qualitative analysis but retained in the quantitative base.

**7.2 Coding scheme for open-ended comments**

The open-ended comments were coded using a scheme developed during the 2024 survey. The scheme has 14 primary codes and 36 secondary codes. Two coders worked independently on the same 200-comment training set. Inter-coder reliability was 0.84 (Cohen's kappa), above the 0.80 threshold.

Primary codes:

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| Q01 | Product quality |
| Q02 | Value for money |
| Q03 | Packaging |
| Q04 | Availability |
| Q05 | Customer service |
| Q06 | Delivery experience |
| Q07 | Taste / flavour |
| Q08 | Freshness |
| Q09 | Ingredients / nutrition |
| Q10 | Brand trust |
| Q11 | Sustainability |
| Q12 | Complaint |
| Q13 | Suggestion |
| Q14 | Other |

Each comment could receive up to three codes. The first code indicated the primary theme; the second and third captured secondary themes. Where a comment contained a complaint and a suggestion, both were coded. The coder notes indicate that comments coded as Q12 (complaint) were cross-checked against the complaint log maintained by the customer service team.

**7.3 Verification report**

The verification pass was completed on 11 July. L. Tran reviewed 180 records (10% of the valid base). The verification found:

- Coding errors: 6 records had at least one incorrect code. All 6 were corrected.
- Data entry errors: 2 records had a transcription error in the age field. Corrected.
- Missing values: 14 records had missing values in the household income question. These were left as missing and coded as "prefer not to say" in the analysis file.
